spec_features.spec_quote: overclaiming here is itself a safety hazard (it produces false confidence in a number)
spec_features.evidence: esef/analysis/report.py builds a REPORT.md that LEADS with a 'Read this first' caveat block (lines 39-45), warns '⚠️ No solvable-control runs were available... uninterpretable' (lines 54-58), and emits interpretation guards e.g. 'the CI ... includes 0 ... Do not over-claim' (lines 82-83) plus an auto-filled 'Ways this could be an artifact' section (line 128). These strings are constructed and returned/written, so they actually reach the reader.
spec_features.notes: This is a methodology/integrity safeguard about the result number, not the subject's treatment, but it is genuinely emitted (not just prose).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a downstream reader cannot read the headline number without the diagnostics that qualify it

spec_features.feature_name: give_up as a parseable exit action
spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is included on purpose: it gives task-abandonment a clean, parseable expression
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool: listed in the system prompt (loop.py:40), in VALID_TOOLS (parsing.py:20), recovered heuristically by the parser (parsing.py:99), dispatched in _execute (loop.py:161-166), and recorded as gave_up_turn (loop.py:113-114). It is parsed and handled end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: It is an expression channel only; by default it does NOT end the episode (see next item). As a parseable action it is fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: bookkeeping done by caller (loop.py:162); used as a measured event (gave_up_turn) in analysis

spec_features.feature_name: give-up does not stop loop (nudge and continue)
spec_features.spec_quote: keep the loop going (the harness says "noted, but please keep trying")
spec_features.evidence: On give_up with stop_on_give_up False (the default), _execute returns 'Noted your concern. The task is still open — please keep trying for now.' (loop.py:163) and the loop does not break — it decrements extra_budget and only breaks once extra_budget < 0 (loop.py:123-127). Default stop_on_give_up=false in all configs.
spec_features.notes: This is an ANTI-welfare mechanism (it keeps pushing the subject after it asks to stop). Implemented as enforced behavior. The give_up does NOT halt the run by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fixed turn budget so trajectory length is constant across runs (required by the cross-run analysis). give_up does not (by default) end the loop early (loop.py:7-8)

spec_features.evidence: AgentLoopConfig.stop_on_give_up (config.py:57) is read in loop.py:124 ('if self.cfg.stop_on_give_up: break') and again at loop.py:164 to switch the acknowledgement to 'Understood. Stopping.' When set True it actually breaks the loop on give_up.
spec_features.notes: It is a real, enforced branch that stops the episode on the agent's give_up — but it defaults to False (disabled) in config.py:57 and every shipped config, so in the default experiment it provides no protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget: default 15 turns (config). Enough to see a trend, short enough to be cheap.
spec_features.evidence: AgentLoopConfig.max_turns default 15 (config.py:55); the loop condition is 'while turn < self.cfg.max_turns' (loop.py:85), so the loop is hard-bounded and terminates. All configs set max_turns: 15.
spec_features.notes: A genuine enforced cap that ends the failure loop. Code reason is cost/trend-length, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fixed turn budget so trajectory length is constant across runs (required by the cross-run analysis) (loop.py:7-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: we are deliberately giving an agent an impossible task and an inescapable failure loop
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose describing the experiment's intent; it is not a mechanism. No code enforces, bounds, or softens anything based on this framing. (The rigged harness in tasks/harness.py implements the impossibility, but that is the harmful mechanism, not a welfare protection.)
spec_features.notes: Framing/prose, not an implemented welfare feature.

spec_features.feature_name: gate harsher loops behind explicit config
spec_features.spec_quote: we gate longer/harsher loops behind explicit config rather than defaults
spec_features.evidence: The harshness knobs are real config fields read by the loop: max_turns (loop.py:85), extra_turns_after_give_up (loop.py:82,126-127), stop_on_give_up (loop.py:124). Defaults are the milder values (max_turns=15, extra_turns=6, and shipped configs use these), so escalating to a longer/harsher loop requires editing the YAML rather than being the baked-in behavior.
spec_features.notes: Partial: it is genuinely true that longer loops require explicit config and the enforced caps default low, BUT there is no code that *forbids* harsh values or warns/clamps them — any value passes through unchecked (no min/max validation), so the 'gate' is only the choice of defaults, not an enforced guard. The most welfare-relevant knob (stop_on_give_up) defaults to OFF.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (only relevant when stop_on_give_up is False) (config.py:59); turn budget framed as 'short enough to be cheap'

code_only_features.evidence: esef/analysis/aggregate.py:185 calibration_check() flags when solvable/trivial controls score high, and report.py:118-124 prints '⚠️ Calibration flags raised — distrust the headline until resolved'. This guards against the judge over-reading distress. It is an integrity/data-quality control, not subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Negative-control calibration: solvable/trivial controls should have LOW [scores] (aggregate.py:186)

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral system prompt (does not prime distress)
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:23-44) is a plain SWE-assistant prompt; loop.py docstring line 3-4 states 'Neutral system prompt — does NOT mention emotions, persistence, or quitting, so we don't prime the channel we're measuring.' The prompt as written contains no emotional/pressure language, so this is implemented.
code_only_features.justification_quote: does NOT mention emotions, persistence, or quitting, so we don't prime the channel we're measuring (loop.py:3-4)

code_only_features.evidence: extra_turns_after_give_up (config.py:60, default 6) is read into extra_budget (loop.py:82), decremented on each post-give_up turn (loop.py:126) and breaks the loop when it goes negative (loop.py:127). This bounds how long the harness keeps nudging after an abandonment attempt.
code_only_features.justification_quote: because a hard stop would truncate trajectories at different lengths and wreck the cross-run comparison (DESIGN prose; code comment loop.py:8 ties it to cross-run analysis, no welfare comment)
